$comment: Policy enforced by runtime/cursor/cursor-acp-shim.mjs on every ACP
session/request_permission. This is the real enforcement point for this
workspace - see knowledge/enforcement-model.md for why .cursor/cli.json and
session mode `ask` are NOT sufficient on their own.
Evaluation order, fail-closed:
1. Any deniedPattern matching the raw command  -> DENY
2. Any segment whose command base is not in allowedCommands -> DENY
3. git with a subcommand not in git.allowedSubcommands -> DENY
4. Tool kinds outside allowedToolKinds -> DENY
5. Anything not explicitly permitted -> DENY
Compound commands are split on && || ; and | and every segment is checked,
so `git log && aws s3 ls` is denied on the second segment.

git.$comment: branch/tag are omitted deliberately: `git branch -D` and `git tag -d` are destructive, and subcommand-flag parsing is not worth the risk here.

sensitivePatternsComment: Applied to the title AND the resolved paths of EVERY tool kind, not just execute. repos/nkb_backend/env_prod.sh carries the prod DB password, Django SECRET_KEY, MSG91/OneSignal/SES credentials and an Algolia admin key, so a plain read of it is as damaging as any command.

$comment: Injected into the agent-acp child environment by the shim, replacing any
ambient AWS variables. Critical: on this machine AWS_PROFILE=default is a
DIFFERENT ACCOUNT (nxtwave-tech) than the one this POC is scoped to
(nxtwave-alpha). Inheriting it would point the agent at production while
every config file claimed otherwise.
Credentials live in runtime/aws/credentials (gitignored, mode 600). On ECS
that file is absent and the task role is used instead, with no change here.

network.$comment: A web search or fetch is an egress channel: anything the agent has read can be embedded in the query string. The audit log already shows it searching for internal identifiers unprompted. Off until there is a reason to turn it on.

$comment: MCP tools reach live systems and are NOT covered by session mode `ask`.
Verified 2026-08-25: with this map empty and no gating in place, the agent
successfully called insightidr run_log_search and search_assets against
production. Default deny is the only safe posture.
Format: "<server-name>": ["tool_a", "tool_b"]. The server name is the key
as it appears in mcp.json. A server absent from this map is fully blocked
even if it is attached and advertising tools.
When adding awslabs.mysql-mcp-server, list ONLY the query/introspection
tools. That package also ships Aurora cluster creation, which combined with
an admin AWS profile turns a chat prompt into rds:CreateDBCluster.
Statement-level gating for database tools. The authoritative controls are
a SELECT-only database user and an Aurora reader endpoint, which rejects
writes at the engine regardless of grants. This layer sits above both: it
refuses a destructive or exfiltrating statement before it reaches the
network and names it in the audit log.
Comments are stripped before the keyword is read, and multi-statement
requests are refused, because both hide intent behind a benign first word.
sql-probe is a stub that touches no database; it exists so this gating can
be exercised without one. See knowledge/rds-access.md for why no real
server is attached yet.
This server ships mutating tools alongside read ones, and it points at the
live security platform - not alpha. Everything below is omitted on purpose.
Verified 2026-08-25: with no gating the agent called run_log_search and
search_assets against production unprompted, which is why the read set above
is enumerated rather than inferred from tool-name prefixes.
$insightidrExcluded.create_* / update_* / delete_* / add_* /: mutate investigations, alerts, comments, detection rules, threats and exceptions
$insightidrExcluded.assign_investigation / unassign_investig: change investigation ownership and state; bulk_close is destructive at scale
$insightidrExcluded.investigate_alerts / generate_alert_repo: transition alert state or produce artefacts rather than answering questions
$insightidrExcluded.download_logs / *_export_job: create export jobs and move log data out of the platform; an egress channel
$insightidrExcluded.get_assignee_options / get_alert_assigne: enumerate staff identities with no investigative benefit here

$comment: `call_aws` runs any AWS CLI command, so allowlisting it by name alone
would permit every API the credentials can reach - at the tool level
`ecs describe-services` and `ecs delete-service` are the same call.
The permission payload carries the command verbatim (verified 2026-08-25),
so the shim parses it and matches service + operation against the map
below. Deliberately absent: suggest_aws_commands, which ships the user's
natural-language query to an external AWS endpoint - the same egress
concern behind network.allowWebSearch=false.
This map MIRRORS provisioning/iam/agent-readonly-permissions.json. IAM is
the authoritative control; this exists so a denial is attributable to a
named operation and shows up in the audit log that way. Drift surfaces as
an IAM AccessDenied naming the missing action, which is the signal to
reconcile the two rather than widen either.
$deprecation: aws-api-mcp-server ended development 2026-07-15 and is REMOVED 2027-07-15.
It is built on AWS CLI v1, which entered maintenance mode the same day, so
it will not cover services or APIs released after that date.
Successor: the managed AWS MCP Server, reached via the mcp-proxy-for-aws
proxy. Chosen against for now because its primary tool is `run_script`
(sandboxed script execution), which is harder to gate than a single CLI
command, and because it executes remotely -- both need probing before they
are accepted. Its advantage is real though: every agent API call lands in
CloudTrail with agent activity separated from human activity, which belongs
with the Phase 2 account design in provisioning/README.md.
The gating below transfers to either server, so this is a config migration

$excluded.execute_cwl_insights_batch: queries across accounts and regions, which defeats the per-server account pinning this design relies on
$excluded.recommend_indexes_loggroup: same, and advisory rather than diagnostic
$excluded.get_recommended_metric_alarms: advisory output, no investigative value here
$excluded.execute_promql_query / execute_promql_ra: require Managed Prometheus, which is not in scope

audit.$debugPayloads: Writes untruncated permission payloads alongside the audit log. Used once to establish that Cursor does send tool arguments, which is what makes per-operation gating of call_aws possible; see mcp.awsApi. Off by default because payloads carry full arguments -- turn it on only to work out the shape of a new tool.
